title: Sim-to-Real Transfer of Robotic Control with Dynamics Randomization
source_version: arXiv:1710.06537v3, revised 2018-03-03; all evidence locators use this PDF

claims.statement: For puck pushing, Table II reports LSTM success of 0.91 +/- 0.03 in simulation and 0.89 +/- 0.06 on the real robot, with 100 simulation trials and 28 real trials.

evidence_locator.table_or_figure: Table II, LSTM row and caption; Figure 7

claims.unsupported_extension: Does not establish equal performance across arbitrary robots or manipulation tasks.

claims.statement: Table III reports lower real-robot success for fixed action timing and omitted observation noise than for the all-parameters condition.

evidence_locator.table_or_figure: Table III, all / fixed action timestep / no observation noise rows

claims.scope: Reported LSTM ablations on the real Fetch arm.
claims.unsupported_extension: Does not establish universal causal effect sizes or a formal significance test.

claims.statement: Dynamics parameters are sampled at episode start; mass and damping remain fixed within an episode, while action timing and observation noise vary at individual timesteps.
claims.unsupported_extension: Do not infer that every random quantity stays fixed throughout an episode.

retrieval_queries.query: Which simulated properties stay unchanged during one rollout, and which disturbances are redrawn while the controller runs?
